facts.text: Validation status CAUTION. The numbers passed the integrity checks (internally consistent); CAUTION means they can be interpreted only with the cautions below. No status, including PASS, is a clinical or real-world validation.

CAUTION Imprecise estimates: For some outcomes the 95% interval is wide compared with the baseline level, so the size of the change is uncertain. Detail: CI half-width exceeds 25% of the baseline level for: stage_space_wait_mean. Estimates are too imprecise to support conclusions.

CAUTION Lopsided differences: For some outcomes a few simulated weeks differ much more than the rest, so the 95% interval is less reliable than usual. Detail: Paired differences are strongly skewed (|skew| > 2) for: los_p90_admitted, boarding_p90, stage_space_wait_mean, stage_results_mean, stage_boarding_mean; the normal approximation behind the t interval is less reliable.

CAUTION Overloaded weeks (stress test): In at least one simulated week queues kept growing; results there describe a stress test, not ordinary operation. Detail: Overloaded replications: {'baseline': 1, 'add_evening_physician': 1}. Effects here describe a STRESS-TEST regime (queues growing with run length), not ordinary operation.

CAUTION Cautions from individual weeks: Individual simulated weeks carried their own cautions (for example model assumptions, extreme waits, or delays for the most urgent patients). Detail: Replication-level CAUTION checks (count across both arms): capacity_and_stability x60, esi1_timeliness x29, extreme_waits x4, model_assumptions x60, no_bottleneck_claims x60, single_seed x60
CAUTION Model-only evidence: The evidence comes from inside the fictional model and cannot support conclusions about real hospitals. Detail: evidence is internal to the fictional model.
Capacity and stability (in 60 simulated weeks across both arms): Demand is close to or above capacity, so queues may grow during the week.
Most urgent patients (in 29 simulated weeks across both arms): Some ESI 1 patients waited longer than an illustrative review threshold because the model does not let them pre-empt other patients.
Extreme waits (in 4 simulated weeks across both arms): Some simulated patients waited far longer than typical, which the averages may hide.
Model assumptions (in 60 simulated weeks across both arms): Results depend on illustrative assumptions that have not been checked against any real ED.
No bottleneck claims (in 60 simulated weeks across both arms): A single run cannot show which constraint truly limits flow.
One random seed (in 60 simulated weeks across both arms): A single simulated week is one random draw; only averages across many weeks are compared.

Each arm was simulated on the same 30 random seeds (paired weeks of 8 arrival days, 1 warm-up day). Pairing removes much, but not all, of the week-to-week random variation from the comparison; the 95% confidence interval describes the remaining uncertainty about the average change across simulated weeks.

Model-internal evidence only: confidence intervals describe the fictional model's behavior across random seeds under its stated assumptions. They are not evidence about any real hospital, and no intervention is shown to be clinically safe.
FICTIONAL MODEL: results describe the fictional Riverside Commons ED under illustrative assumptions. They are not clinically validated and do not describe any real hospital.
NOT A STAFFING RECOMMENDATION: no simulated result establishes that a staffing or capacity change would be safe in a real ED. Decisions require qualified human review.

ESI-1 PRIORITY LIMITATION: priority is non-preemptive. A critically ill (ESI 1) patient waits for the next free physician or space instead of receiving immediate resuscitation, so the model can understate how fast critical patients are seen.
TRIAGE IS FIRST COME, FIRST SERVED: acuity priority applies only after triage, so higher-acuity patients wait in the same triage line as everyone else.

PHYSICIAN CONCURRENCY IS FICTIONAL: each physician is assumed to evaluate up to 2 patients at once. Results are highly sensitive to this assumption; the Milestone 6 sensitivity analysis varies it (1-3) and flags conclusions that change with it.

BED RELEASES ARE A SIMPLIFIED ABSTRACTION: inpatient beds open for the ED at an assumed rate (42/day, afternoon-weighted). It is not derived from bed counts or occupancy, and boarding results depend heavily on it.

LEFT WITHOUT BEING SEEN IS NOT MODELED: every simulated patient waits to be seen, so no LWBS rate is reported and waits for the most crowded periods may be overstated relative to a real ED where some patients leave.
